title: How the Whale Got His Throat
blurb: A clever sailor is swallowed whole and refuses to be quiet.
script:
[warmly] Long, long ago… in the sea, there was a Whale, and he ate fishes.

[excited] He ate the starfish and the garfish, and the crab and the dab, and the plaice and the dace, and the mackerel and the pickerel, and the REALLY truly twirly eel.

[amused] He ate all the fishes he could find in all the sea… until at last there was only one small fish left. [playfully] And that one was a clever little Fish, who swam just behind the Whale's right ear, where he could not be reached.

[curious] “Are you not hungry?” said the small clever Fish.

[grandly] “I am,” said the Whale. “What shall I eat now?”

[mischievously] “Have you ever tasted Man?” said the Fish.

[curious] “What is it like?” said the Whale.

[amused] “Nice,” said the Fish. “Nice… but nubbly. There is one sitting on a raft in the middle of the sea, with nothing on but a pair of blue canvas trousers and a jack-knife. [whispers] But I ought to tell you — he is a man of infinite resource and sagacity.”

[excited] So the Whale swam and swam, as fast as his fins could take him, and he found the raft.

[loudly] And he opened his mouth wide, and wider, and wider still, until it nearly touched his tail — [short pause] and he swallowed the shipwrecked Mariner, and the raft he was sitting on, and his blue canvas trousers, and the jack-knife.

[amused] He swallowed them all down into his warm dark inside cupboards. [playfully] And then he smacked his lips, and turned round three times on his tail.

[curious] But the moment the Mariner found himself inside the Whale, he did something the Whale did not expect at all.

[playfully] He began to jump. [excited] He hopped and he skipped. He stepped and he lepped. He danced hornpipes where he shouldn't. And he beat his heels upon the walls.

[worried] And the Whale began to feel VERY unhappy indeed.

“This man is nubbly,” said the Whale, “and he gives me the hiccups. [firmly] Mariner, come out, and behave yourself.”

[calmly] “Not so,” said the Mariner from somewhere deep inside. “Take me home to my own white cliffs of Albion… [firmly] and I will think about it.”

[sad] And he began to dance harder than ever.

[calmly] So the Whale swam, and he swam, with both flippers and his tail, as hard as he could for the hiccups. And at last he saw the Mariner's white cliffs, and he rushed halfway up the beach, and opened his mouth wide, and wider, and wider still.

[excited] “Change here for England!” he said.

[amused] And out walked the Mariner. But while he had been inside, he had cut up his raft with his jack-knife into a little square grating, all criss-cross… [mischievously] and he had tied it into the Whale's throat with his blue canvas trousers.

[surprised] And the Whale swallowed — and could not.

[amused] The grating stuck fast. And from that day to this, the Whale has never been able to eat anything bigger than very, very small fish.

[warmly] Which is why, if ever you meet a whale, you will find he does not eat men, or little girls, or little boys. [gently] He simply cannot. There is a raft in the way.
